rows.body: Confirm with brand for agreement year

Upscale brands under the Choice portfolio typically share central reservations, loyalty, and reporting while maintaining distinct guestroom and public-space standards. Owners should treat requirements as agreement- and prototype-specific: conversion from a sister flag may reduce scope, but upscale positioning (including Alpha Brand Studios cues where applicable) can still trigger design, FF&E, and QA obligations beyond a light reflag.

rows.title: Brand Identity & Guest Experience
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Arrival, lobby, corridor, and in-room touchpoints are usually aligned to the active standards manual for the signing vintage—signage families, scent, music, and service rituals may be prescribed.
Owner planning consideration: Map which elements are mandatory at opening vs. within a post-opening compliance window; budget for brand-approved vendors where specified.
Applies to: New build, conversion, and reflag
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Flexibility / exception notes: Sister-flag conversions may reuse certain FF&E or signage with written waivers.

rows.title: Guestroom, Bath & Sleep Experience
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Room modules, casegoods, lighting, and bath specifications are often tied to approved prototypes; mattress and linen programs are usually mandated.
Owner planning consideration: Lead times for casegoods and bath packages drive opening dates; partial conversions may require room-type-by-room PIP schedules.
Applies to: All guest-facing projects
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Flexibility / exception notes: Soft conversions may defer non-visible items only with brand approval.

rows.title: Public Space, Lobby & Upscale Positioning
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Lobby zoning, meeting pre-function, and social spaces may need to reflect upscale positioning—furniture families, art, and digital guest messaging are commonly controlled.
Owner planning consideration: Ceiling heights, storefront, and co-tenancy rules affect entitlement; upscale refresh can exceed select-service conversion cost.
Applies to: New build and conversion
Typical status: Confirm with brand

rows.title: Food, Beverage & Social Spaces
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Restaurant, bar, or enhanced market concepts may be required or optional by prototype; kitchen exhaust, hood, and liquor scope vary by market.
Owner planning consideration: Operator model (self-op vs. lease), daypart staffing, and brand F&B audits should be modeled before LOI.
Applies to: Properties with in-scope F&B
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Flexibility / exception notes: Contract F&B operators still typically require brand concept approval.

rows.title: Meetings, Events & Group Business
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Meeting room counts, divisible walls, AV standards, and group sales tooling may be specified for upscale urban and suburban prototypes.
Owner planning consideration: Load-in, ballroom stack, and telecom backbone affect core-and-shell; group mix assumptions tie to brand sales support.
Applies to: Hotels with meeting inventory
Typical status: Confirm with brand

rows.title: Technology, CRS & Loyalty Programs
rows.body:
Typical consideration: PMS, CRS, Wi-Fi, digital key, and guest apps are typically prescribed; Choice portfolio connectivity and loyalty enrollment are usually mandatory at cutover.
Owner planning consideration: Plan parallel runs, data migration, and channel-manager mapping to avoid double bookings and rate parity issues.
Applies to: All operating hotels
Typical status: Contractual cutover date in agreement
Flexibility / exception notes: Legacy systems on conversion are often allowed for a limited transition period only.

rows.title: Design Review, Plans & Submittals
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Architectural, interior, and MEP submittals usually pass through brand design review with milestone gates before construction.
Owner planning consideration: Budget design review fees, consultant rework cycles, and schedule float for resubmittals.
Applies to: New build and material renovation
Typical status: Confirm with brand
Flexibility / exception notes: Abbreviated review may be available for recent sister-flag renovations—document in writing.

rows.title: PIP, Conversion & Sister-Flag Transitions
rows.body:
Typical consideration: PIP line items are often itemized by FF&E, soft goods, signage, and technology; scope may be lighter when retaining compatible assets from the same parent.
Owner planning consideration: Tie PIP funding to incentive package; separate mandatory opening items from 12–24 month deferrals in LOI discussions.
Applies to: Conversion and reflag
Typical status: Often negotiated
Flexibility / exception notes: Prior PIP completion within 24–36 months may reduce scope—confirm eligibility.

rows.title: QA, Inspection & Ongoing Compliance
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Pre-opening inspection, annual QA, and mystery-guest programs may apply with scored remediation and reinspection fees.
Owner planning consideration: Reserve management time and capital for action plans; understand fee exposure for repeat failures.
Applies to: Opening and stabilized operations
Typical status: Confirm with brand

rows.title: Sustainability, Accessibility & Life Safety
rows.body:
Typical consideration: Brand sustainability playbooks and accessibility targets may exceed local code; life safety and brand fire-life-safety reviews are typically non-negotiable.
Owner planning consideration: Early coordination on EV charging, water programs, and accessible room dispersion; do not assume code compliance alone satisfies brand.
Applies to: New build and renovation
Typical status: Confirm with brand

When moving within the Choice family, owners often sequence loyalty cutover, CRS/PMS migration, signage, and soft-goods refresh before a full public-space rebuild. Confirm whether Radisson upscale positioning under Alpha Brand Studios adds mandatory design elements beyond the prior flag, and whether any items from a recent sister-brand PIP can carry forward with waivers.

What QA and inspection fees apply at opening and annually?
What upscale positioning elements are mandatory vs. recommended for this sub-brand tier?

Are parent-level sustainability or accessibility addenda in force for this agreement?
